statement: Ṛgveda 10.129 treats cosmic origins as a problem rather than presenting a single confident mechanism: it evokes darkness/waters and closes by questioning whether even the highest overseer knows how creation arose.

sources.citation: Joel P. Brereton, “Edifying Puzzlement: Ṛgveda 10.129 and the Uses of Enigma.” Journal of the American Oriental Society 119.2 (1999): 248–260.
sources.author: Joel P. Brereton
sources.venue: Journal of the American Oriental Society

sources.citation: The Ancient Languages of Asia and the Americas, chapter “Sanskrit” (Cambridge University Press, 2008), on Ṛgvedic chronology and oral transmission.

does_not_demonstrate: Motif similarity with another tradition does not by itself demonstrate borrowing, common ancestry, or direct transmission.
